issues.display_title: Issue #514: Floor list order, Preview/Live floor dropdown, and View 360 Pano modal (PRD #496)
issues.main_description_html:
From PRD #496 — floor navigation consistency and 360 pano modal restyle. UI designs: #511 (floor selector) and #512 (pano modal), implemented on design/modal-improvements.

Description

FE targets (per anurdin01 on #496):

  • Floor list order — highest floor at the top, Level 1 / Ground / closest-to-ground at the bottom, consistent across Editor, Map Mode, Preview, and Live modes, matching the Level Edit Modal
  • Preview & Live floor selector — replace the full floor list with a compact dropdown next to the Direction button; default active floor is Floor 1 / Ground / closest-to-ground
  • View 360 Pano modal — restyle to match the floor plan image / photo information preview modals: title "View 360 Pano" plus the related information title, no pagination or page counters

Work is integration of the design/modal-improvements branch (df8439c) into development.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Editor and Map Mode level lists ordered highest → lowest, ground at the bottom, matching the Level Edit Modal
  • Preview and Live use a floor dropdown next to the Direction button (no full floor list), ordered highest → lowest
  • Preview and Live start on Floor 1 / Ground / closest-to-ground; selecting a floor changes the active floor; Direction button still works
  • View 360 Pano modal matches the existing preview modal style: "View 360 Pano" title, related information title, no pagination or page counters, works on desktop/tablet/mobile
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Done on feature/514-floor-order-dropdown-pano-modal — integration of design/modal-improvements (df8439c) into a branch cut from development, merge commit 8ace2c4 + fixup 639d168.

  • src/lib/editor/levels.ts — highestFirst() (stored order reversed: highest floor first, ground at the bottom) + publicDefaultLevelId() (entry floor = first canonical level)
  • src/components/editor/floorOptions.ts — buildFloorOptions() merges floor configs with canvas levels, ordered highest → lowest; used by EditorPanel (editor level list) and FloorSelector (map mode)
  • src/components/editor/preview/PreviewControls.tsx — compact floor dropdown in the ordered control row next to the Direction button, for Preview and Live modes
  • src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx — uses publicDefaultLevelId so Preview/Live start on the closest-to-ground floor; replaced the full floor list with PreviewControls
  • src/components/editor/preview/PanoModal.tsx — restyled to match the floor plan/photo preview modals: "View 360 Pano" title, related information title, no pagination or page counters
  • Fixup 639d168: coalesce string | null store projectId to undefined for the PreviewControls prop (tsc error after merge)

Verification: 646 tests passed (5 new test files from the design branch), lint clean, tsc --noEmit clean.

Not pushed yet — awaiting approval to push + merge to development.

issues.display_title: Issue #515: Editor Edit Floors button opens the wizard Edit Floor modal with drag-and-drop reorder; retire the old level-list modal
issues.main_description_html:
The editor's Edit Floors button currently opens the old level-list modal (EditLevelModal), which nests the wizard-style EditFloorModal behind a settings icon. It should open the wizard-style modal directly — but that modal has no drag-and-drop floor reordering, so reordering must be added to it first.

Description

  • Add drag-and-drop floor reordering to EditFloorModal (wizard Step 3 "Edit Floor" surface), reusing the existing useFloorReorder hook + grip pattern from the wizard FloorList (mouse, keyboard, and screen-reader announcements included). Display order stays bottom-up (ground at the bottom).
  • Editor's Edit Floors button opens EditFloorModal directly. EditLevelModal becomes a thin editor wrapper (store glue only: config seeding, delete with floormap file cleanup, floor settings) — its old list UI is removed.
  • Reorder in the editor must commit the new order to canvasData.levels via levelsInConfigOrder (issue #470 — config-only reorder diverges the 3D stack, FloorSelector, and preview/live).
  • Wizard Step 3 passes its existing reorder handler so the modal reorders there too.

Known trade-off: the old modal's per-floor change/remove image and image preview actions are not part of the wizard-style modal and are dropped with it.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Editor Edit Floors button opens the wizard-style Edit Floor modal directly (settings bar, name/height fields, delete, Ground divider)
  • Floors can be reordered by dragging in the modal, in editor and wizard contexts; keyboard reorder works
  • Editor reorder updates canvasData.levels order (3D stack, floor selector, preview/live stay in sync) and is undoable
  • Old level-list modal UI is removed
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Done on feature/515-edit-floor-modal-dnd, commit 70a8988. Net −233 lines.

  • src/components/setup/step-list-floor/EditFloorModal.tsx — new required onReorder prop; reordering via the existing useFloorReorder hook (same as wizard FloorList): drag with insertion-line indicator, ArrowUp/ArrowDown keyboard moves with focus-follow, screen-reader announcements. Only the grip is draggable, so text selection in the name/height inputs never starts a row drag.
  • src/components/editor/EditLevelModal.tsx — old level-list modal UI deleted (463 → 113 lines); now a thin editor wrapper that renders EditFloorModal directly with editor glue: floorConfig seeding for imported levels, delete via deleteLevel + floormap file cleanup, and exported commitFloorOrder which syncs the new order into canvasData.levels via levelsInConfigOrder (#470) in one undoable history snapshot. EditorPanel untouched (same import).
  • src/components/setup/StepListFloor.tsx — passes its existing reorder handler, so the wizard's Edit Floor modal reorders too.
  • Tests: 3 new in EditLevelModal.test.ts covering the #470 commit path (configs + canvasData sync, no-op on unchanged order, null canvasData). Suite 649 passed; lint + tsc --noEmit clean.

Trade-off (flagged in Description): the old modal's per-floor change/remove image and image preview actions are dropped with it.

Not pushed yet — awaiting approval to push + merge to development.

  • src/lib/projects/emptyProject.ts + its test (add/add) — keep the development version; it backs the already-shipped functional flow

Functional behavior (validation, creation flow, floor seeding, no predict call) must stay as shipped; this task lands the visual layer.

Acceptance Criteria

  • New Project opens the designed choice modal (AI Scanning Floor / Create Empty Project) per #448
  • Create Empty Project modal matches the design; existing validation and creation flow unchanged
  • Empty floor in the editor shows the designed empty-canvas state per #452

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Done on feature/516-empty-project-ui, merge commit 8490142 (design e5bd201 reconciled onto development).

  • NewProjectFlow.tsx — designed choice modal (Scan a floor plan / Start from an empty canvas) + create-empty stage with address autocomplete, lat/lng validation, and origin-pin map. Submit rewired to the shipped flow: createProject → /editor/<id>?empty=1 (editor seeds the blank floor, #451) — the design branch's client-side snapshot writes (createEmptyProjectSnapshot/updateProject/saveFloorplanAction) were dropped. Default map view uses the shared wizard coordinates.

  • EmptyCanvasPointer.tsx (#452) — anchors to the Add Wall tool on an empty floor. The editor page sets a session flag before it strips ?empty=1 post-seed (router.replace), and the pointer reads the URL or that flag — otherwise it would vanish immediately.
  • emptyProject.ts kept as the development version, extended with parseCoordinate / validProjectName / levelHasGeometry.
  • Merge conflicts resolved: dashboard/page.tsx (kept NewProjectFlow wiring), emptyProject.ts + test (kept development). #446 publish-status guard in EditorTopbar survived; floor-plan image toolbar controls now hide when the floor has no backdrop.

issues.display_title: Issue #517: Access object model: floor span, synced connected copies, lift/stair migration (PRD #513)
issues.main_description_html:
From PRD #513 — part 1 of 4. Data model + sync logic for Access objects (lifts and stairs), replacing lift/stair area-type linking.

Description

  • Add Access as the object model for vertical circulation, type: lift | stair
  • Floor span is a multi-select floor list; selecting floors creates connected Access copies on those floors, unselecting removes them
  • Connected copies stay synchronized: type changes, Information link/unlink, and deletion apply to the whole connected group
  • Existing lift/stair area data still loads and migrates safely to Access
  • Access data persists across save, reload, preview, publish, live

Acceptance Criteria

  • Access object type with Lift/Stair variant and connected-group identity
  • Multi-select floor span creates/removes connected copies
  • Type, information link, and deletion propagate to every connected copy
  • Legacy lift/stair area projects load and migrate without data loss
  • Persistence round-trip (save/reload/publish) covered by unit tests
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Done on feature/517-access-object-model, commit f2333e9.

Design: Access = every area sharing an accessId across floors. availableLevelIds is kept as a derived cache of the group's floor span — existing multi-level routing keeps working unchanged on migrated AND legacy data (routing switches to groups in #520).

  • src/lib/editor/access.ts — pure helpers: accessMembers/accessSpan/accessAdjacent (directly-below/above only), withAccessType/withAccessInfo/withAccessSpan/withoutAccess, and migrateLegacyAccess (mutually linked same-type areas merge nearest-first 1:1 per floor pair via union-find; unmatched areas become standalone groups and keep their legacy links so inconsistent old data routes exactly as before)
  • editorSlice — new setAccessType / setAccessInfo / setAccessFloorSpan / deleteAccess; setAreaType assigns an accessId when an area becomes lift/stairs, propagates vertical type changes group-wide, and detaches the copy when it leaves the vertical types; setAreaInfo, unlinkObjectInfo, linkInfoToObjects propagate Information links to every connected copy
  • Migration wired into both hydrate paths: hydratePersistedState (editor restore, preview, live) and the editor DB restore in useWizardPersistence
  • bridge.ts preserves accessId across the canvas-engine round-trip; AreaLayer.accessId added to store + digitalTwin schema types

Tests: 12 new in access.test.ts (migration merge/nearest/standalone/mixed, span create/remove/no-op, sync helpers, adjacency) + 6 new in useMapStore-vertical.test.ts (store-level propagation); legacy vertical tests untouched and green. Suite 667 passed, lint + tsc --noEmit clean.

Not pushed yet — parts 2–4 (#518–#520) stack on this branch; push + merge approval at the end.

issues.display_title: Issue #518: Editor UI for Access objects: toolbar tool, object-list grouping, floor-span editor (PRD #513)
issues.main_description_html:
From PRD #513 — part 2 of 4. Editor surfaces for the Access model (part 1).

Description

  • Toolbar: new Access tool to place an Access object and choose Lift or Stair
  • Object list: Access grouping; rows show icon, name, type, delete action, and adjacent floor relationships (only the floor directly below and above)
  • Floor span configured only through the Access editor (multi-select floor list)
  • View-only collaborators can inspect Access objects without edit/delete controls

Acceptance Criteria

  • Access tool in the editor toolbar creates an Access object with Lift/Stair choice
  • Object list has an Access group: icon, name, type, delete, adjacent floors (below/above only)
  • Floor span multi-select drives connected copies (model from part 1)
  • Deleting from the list removes the whole connected group
  • Viewer role sees Access rows read-only
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Done on feature/518-access-editor-ui (stacked on #517), commit 23f8adb.

  • src/components/editor/panel/AccessList.tsx — Access rows for the active floor: lift/stair icon (custom stairs SVG — lucide has none), name, type label, adjacent floors (directly below/above only, via accessAdjacent), Lift/Stair toggle (setAccessType, group-wide), inline floor-span editor (checkbox per floor → setAccessFloorSpan creates/removes connected copies; the last floor can't be unchecked — delete is the explicit path), and confirm-guarded deleteAccess showing how many floors it removes. Viewer role renders the same rows with no edit affordances.
  • objectFilters.tsx — new "Access" filter entry (ArrowUpDown icon); ObjectSection.tsx routes it to AccessList in both editor and viewer roles and counts access areas from layout.areas.
  • Access creation rides the existing flow: draw an area, set its type to Lift/Stairs in the selection toolbar — #517's setAreaType assigns the group identity. No separate drawing tool was added (the area-type radio already covers "create + choose Lift or Stair").

Tests: 5 new RTL tests in AccessList.test.tsx (listing + adjacency, span extend, group delete, group retype, viewer read-only). Suite 672 passed, lint + tsc --noEmit clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #520: Multi-floor directions through nearest valid Access, unavailable state, route z-order (PRD #513)
issues.main_description_html:
From PRD #513 — part 4 of 4. Routing improvements on top of the Access model (part 1).

Description

  • Cross-floor directions route through usable Access objects (multiLevelRoute.ts / pathfinder.ts)
  • When multiple Access paths exist, choose the nearest valid one
  • Clear unavailable state when no Access path connects the floors
  • Route lines render above ghost/reference walls
  • Same-floor directions unchanged; editor preview, standalone preview, and live behave consistently

Acceptance Criteria

  • Cross-floor route passes through the nearest valid Access object
  • No-path case shows an explicit unavailable state (no silent failure)
  • Same-floor routing regression-free
  • Route lines readable above ghost/reference walls
  • Consistent behavior in editor preview, /preview/[projectId], and /v/[key]
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Done on feature/520-access-routing (stacked on #519), commit ac40312.

  • multiLevelRoute.ts — Access-aware connector pairing: a grouped origin connector's arrival pool is its own connected copy (same physical shaft) instead of any lift/stair serving the same floor pair, which could previously "teleport" a rider into a different shaft across the building. Ungrouped legacy connectors keep the old any-pair matching, so unmigrated data routes exactly as before. Nearest-valid selection (shortest first+second leg) and the explicit unavailable statuses (no-connector, missing-destination-connector, blocked-walk — already surfaced by DirectionPanel) are unchanged.
  • useFloorPlanLabels.ts — the direction route line draws a white halo under the blue stroke, keeping it readable over ghost/reference walls and dense geometry. The line renders on the 2D canvas overlay, which is always above the WebGL map layers, in editor preview, standalone preview, and live alike (all three share PreviewOverlay).
  • Same-floor routing untouched.

Tests: 2 new in multiLevelRoute.test.ts — grouped connectors refuse cross-shaft arrivals (blocked instead of teleporting), legacy ungrouped keep any-pair matching; the 7 existing routing tests (nearest choice, statuses, same-floor, point endpoints) still pass. Suite 676 passed, lint + tsc --noEmit clean.

Not pushed yet — chain #517→#520 complete, awaiting push + merge approval.
